claims.explanation: JZL-184 is a covalent inhibitor of monoacylglycerol lipase (MGLL/MAGL), the enzyme that degrades 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG); in cancer cells MAGL also supplies free fatty acids for prostaglandin and lysophosphatidic acid synthesis, so lines that depend on MAGL-driven lipid signaling should be selectively killed. The strongest predictor is therefore high MGLL expression (sensitizing), with low MGLL or high alternative lipase/endocannabinoid tone being protective; the hepatocellular carcinoma literature directly links MAGL levels to malignancy and JZL-184 sensitivity.

features.basis: MAGL is the drug target; high MAGL expression predicts dependence and JZL-184 sensitivity in HCC (PMID 27767105)
loss-of-function mutations in the drug target would abolish JZL-184 binding and activity
JZL-184 effects are CB1-receptor mediated via elevated 2-AG (PMID 22924700, 24911644)
2-AG also signals through CB2, contributing to MAGL-inhibitor effects
MAGL-derived arachidonate feeds COX-2/PGE2 signaling in tumors (PMID 27767105)
high FAAH can compensate by degrading endocannabinoids, reducing dependence on MAGL
DGL-alpha synthesizes the 2-AG substrate that MAGL inhibition elevates (PMID 23502535)
alternative 2-AG synthetic enzyme; high synthesis increases 2-AG tone when MAGL is blocked
CaMKII inhibits DGL-alpha and lowers 2-AG, opposing JZL-184 action (PMID 23502535)
MAGL supports LPA signaling in HCC; LPA-receptor-high lines may depend on this axis (PMID 27767105)
alternative 2-AG hydrolase can compensate when MAGL is inhibited
alternative 2-AG hydrolase can compensate when MAGL is inhibited
